mig.label: MIG / solid-core with shielding gas
mig.gas: Shielding gas required; use the wire supplier's recommendation and the chart inside the welder door.

flux-cored.label: Self-shielded flux-cored
flux-cored.gas: No external shielding gas for the self-shielded setup described by the manual.

tig.label: DC TIG
tig.gas: 100% argon is specified by the manual.

stick.label: Stick
stick.polarity: DCEP setup shown by the manual

porosity.title: Porosity: small cavities or holes in the bead
porosity.safety: Shut off and disconnect the welder before adjusting, cleaning, or repairing it.

checks.action: Use DCEP for gas-shielded MIG and DCEN for self-shielded flux-cored welding.
Clean the workpiece to bare metal and use wire free of rust, oil, coatings, and residue.
Move the contact tip closer and maintain the procedure's proper contact-tip-to-work distance.
Maintain a steady travel speed.
For MIG only, verify the bottle, regulator, recommended gas, nozzle cleanliness, and flow rate. This check does not apply to self-shielded flux-cored wire.

checks.cause: Gun is too far from the workpiece
checks.action: Correct the gun position and CTWD.

excessive-spatter.title: Excessive spatter
excessive-spatter.safety: Fine spatter is normal. Grainy, large spatter indicates a problem.

checks.action: Clean the workpiece to bare metal and remove oil, coatings, or residue from the wire.
Verify DCEP for MIG or DCEN for self-shielded flux-cored.
For MIG, increase flow, clean the nozzle, and verify CTWD.
Reduce wire-feed speed.
Reduce CTWD.

burn-through.title: Burn-through
burn-through.safety: Practice on scrap of the same thickness before welding the workpiece.

checks.action: Reduce current and/or wire-feed speed.
Increase travel speed and keep it steady.
Reduce wire-feed speed.

wire-feed.title: Wire-feed motor runs but wire does not feed correctly
wire-feed.safety: Shut off the welder, disconnect it from power, and discharge the MIG gun to ground before adjustments.

checks.action: Increase feed pressure incrementally using the drive-tension test on page 17.
Flip or replace the feed roller so the groove matches the wire diameter.
Have a qualified technician inspect and replace damaged parts.
Loosen it until it applies only enough pressure to stop spool overrun.

bird-nest.title: Wire creates a bird's nest
bird-nest.safety: Disconnect power before opening or adjusting the wire-feed compartment.

checks.action: Readjust drive pressure using the page 17 test.
Install the correct tip for the wire diameter.

checks.cause: Gun cable connector is not fully seated
checks.action: Fully insert the connector into the wire-feed mechanism and tighten it as shown on page 13.
Have the liner inspected and replaced.

unstable-arc.title: Unstable welding arc
unstable-arc.safety: Stop welding before checking connections or consumables.

checks.action: Verify wire feed, contact-tip size, liner size, and wear.
Adjust the setting to match the manual and door chart.
Tighten all cable connections and attach the ground clamp to clean bare metal.
Use DCEP for MIG and DCEN for self-shielded flux-cored.
For MIG or TIG, verify the specified gas and flow without exposing O-rings at the connector.

no-power.title: Welder does not function when switched on
no-power.safety: Do not open or service energized equipment. Electrical repairs require a qualified technician.

checks.action: Leave the power switch on and allow the internal fan to cool the welder, then shorten future welding periods.
Verify the outlet and circuit meet the voltage and amperage specifications.
Check that external connections are fully seated; internal trigger repairs require a technician.
Correct the input voltage, then use the rear reset button.
Select the intended welding process.

processGuide.name: Flux-Cored / FCAW
processGuide.productCaveat: Use DCEN and self-shielded flux-cored wire.

processGuide.name: MIG / GMAW
processGuide.productCaveat: Use DCEP. Aluminum requires the optional spool gun.

processGuide.name: Stick / SMAW
processGuide.productCaveat: The manual's setup places the electrode holder in positive and ground in negative.

processGuide.name: DC TIG / GTAW
processGuide.productCaveat: The OmniPro 220 provides DC TIG. It does not provide the AC TIG required for aluminum or magnesium.
